subject: ACME SLO/SLA follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: ACME SLO/SLA follow-up and next steps

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the call today — great discussion. Quick recap and next steps on performance/SLO questions you raised:

- Target latency: you mentioned p95 <= 150ms and p99 <= 300ms for 512-token prompts; we need to confirm at what sequence length you expect these numbers to be measured.
- Throughput & concurrency: initial target of ~200 concurrent requests with average QPS of 120 — we'd like a representative traffic sample.
- Streaming: you'll need chunked streaming (token-level) for real-time UI; noted as a hard requirement.

I've attached a draft SLO/SLA language and a mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align on measurement methodology and remedies.

Immediate next steps:
1) Can you share an anonymized production traffic sample or histograms (latency, seq len distribution) by EOD Friday?
2) Please confirm whether latency should be measured end-to-end (client-observed) or server-side (gateway-to-response). We recommend server-side at the gateway for stable SLI computation but can map to client metrics in reporting.
3) Internal: looping in Rishi for technical feasibility and Lauren for contracts.

Attachments: acme_slo_draft_v2.pdf, mutual_action_plan.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ACME SLO/SLA follow-up and next steps

Marissa,

Thanks for the succinct recap — very helpful. A few answers and clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide an anonymized day-of-week (peak/avg) traffic sample and a histogram of sequence lengths by Friday. Will strip PII.
- Preference: our product team prefers end-to-end (client-observed) latency as the user-facing SLA. That said, we understand server-side SLIs are more stable for measurement. If you can provide both mappings (server-side SLI -> client metric), that would be ideal.
- Reporting cadence: monthly SLI/SLA reports + a weekly alert if p99 breaches more than 3 times in a month.
- Exclusions: we need scheduled maintenance windows documented and an explicit list of exclusions (force majeure, customer-side networking, large-scale internet outages). Also want clarity on how DDOS is treated.

One more ask: for remedies, our procurement team usually requires a clear credit formula (e.g., % monthly credit tied to unavailability thresholds) and a 30-day cure period.

Alex
Head of Platform
ACME Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com | +1 (212) 555-7890
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME SLO/SLA follow-up and next steps

Alex — thanks, that's exactly the level of detail we need. A few clarifications from our side so we can align the draft: 

Measurement methodology suggestion (Redwood recommendation):
- Primary SLI: server-side request latency measured at the gateway post-auth (measured in ms). We compute p50/p95/p99 across 1-minute sliding windows and roll up to hourly/daily/monthly aggregates for SLA reporting.
- Mapping: we'll provide a mapping document so your client-observed latency can be approximated from server-side SLIs (adds average network delta).

Exclusions (draft language):
- Planned maintenance: defined windows communicated 7 days in advance; maintenance during which SLOs do not apply.
- Force majeure and customer-side networking issues.
- Malicious traffic / confirmed DDOS: excluded if mitigations were exercised; we're open to joint investigation clauses.

Remedies (proposed):
- Tiered service credits based on monthly availability. Example: availability >= 99.9%: no credit; 99.0%-99.89%: 5% monthly credit; <99.0%: 15% monthly credit.
- 30-day cure period for non-repeating breaches; formal escalation path in MAP.

I'll attach an updated SLO/SLA snippet (acme_slo_draft_v2.pdf) with the measurement paragraphs and exclusions called out. Lauren, can we flag anything procurement should expect?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME SLO/SLA follow-up and next steps (technical notes)

Looping in a few technical notes from the infra team to make the measurement/acceptance criteria actionable:

- Latency measurement: measuring at the gateway post-auth is fine. We will record server-side timing at ingress (timestamp_received -> timestamp_last_token_sent). For streaming, p99 should account for time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token; we can publish both metrics.
- Concurrency: define as "concurrent active connections" (open streams) — this matters for resource reservation. Throughput (QPS) is a separate load metric.
- Load testing: recommend a staged perf validation in a mirror environment. Suggested acceptance test: 200 concurrent streams with token lengths drawn from your histogram at 95th percentile seq len. Run sustained 30-minute windows and measure p95/p99.
- Caching/efficiency: we can enable prefix/KV caching to lower tail latency for repeated prompts; we should discuss expected cache hit rates in the MAP.
- Canary/fallback: recommend canary rollout with traffic shifting (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and automatic fallback to a higher-latency, lower-cost variant if p99 exceeds threshold during rollout.

Next steps (technical):
- Marissa: can we schedule a perf validation slot next week? I can provision a dedicated test pool.
- Alex: please share the traffic histogram and a sample client observed latency trace if possible.

Rishi
Staff Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Subject: Re: ACME SLO/SLA follow-up and next steps

Team — this looks good and thank you for the level of detail. Confirming a few commitments from ACME side:

- We'll send the anonymized traffic histogram and a short client-side latency trace by EOD Friday.
- Procurement will review the proposed credit formula; expect feedback within 3 business days.
- We agree to the staged canary approach — please propose a schedule for the validation window (Rishi, any times next week that work?).

Also, please add explicit monthly reporting (PDF report + metrics dashboard link) and a weekly alerting hook for p99 spikes in the MAP. For contract language, we will ask legal to add a clause requiring transparency on planned maintenance and a documented process for joint incident review.

Thanks again — next steps: Marissa, can you own scheduling the perf validation and loop in your SRE? We'll aim to have MAP signed and draft SLA language in the contract within two weeks if the perf tests pass.

Regards,
Alex
